messages:
jamie: Heads-up — product wants a 'batching health' panel in Console for rollouts. They want batch size distribution, median/95th batch wait, and per-queue saturation indicators. Can runtime/telemetry owners chime in on what we can reliably emit from the runtime and what the ingestion costs look like?

nora: +1. For UX we want per-model and per-region breakdowns. Are those labels cheap to keep? Also product asked for a heatmap view of saturation over time.

sandeep: From runtime: we already emit a few metrics we can expose to Console: 
- batch_fill_count{model,region,pool} counter (increments when a batch is flushed)
- batch_wait_seconds_bucket{model,region,pool,le} histogram buckets for time between request enqueue and batch dispatch
- batch_size_hist_bucket{model,region,pool,le} histogram buckets for batch sizes
- batch_saturation_ratio{pool,region} gauge (0..1) computed at flush time
We can add labels but need to be careful about cardinality.

jamie: Can you paste PromQL examples we can wire into a Grafana panel? Also what sampling / rollup should telemetry do for high-card models?

sandeep: Sure — rough PromQL we use as starting point:
```
# median batch size by model (5m rate)
histogram_quantile(0.5, sum(rate(batch_size_hist_bucket[5m])) by (le, model))
# p95 batch wait by model (5m rate)
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(batch_wait_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, model))
# fill rate (batches/s) by pool
sum(rate(batch_fill_count[5m])) by (pool)
# saturation (instant gauge) average by pool
avg(batch_saturation_ratio) by (pool)
```
Notes: buckets are emitted every flush; using sum(rate(...)) reduces noise. For the heatmap, you'd plot batch_saturation_ratio over time bucketed by minute.

ashley: telemetry team here — high-card histograms are expensive to ingest and store. For initial Console panels we should: (1) restrict model label to verified models only, (2) roll up to 1m resolution, (3) sample 1% of requests for models with >100qps unless we add aggregation in runtime. That keeps cost reasonable.

nora: UX asks for a saturation heatmap (pool x time) and a small per-model sparkline. If metrics are missing for some pools show a fallback state ("no data — sampling or disabled").

sandeep: We can add a coarse 'saturation_bucket' label if heatmap binning on the backend helps. Alternatively keep batch_saturation_ratio as a gauge and let Grafana bucket it client-side. Backend binning would reduce dashboard queries at the cost of more metric writes.

jamie: OK tradeoffs noted. Proposed action items: 
- jamie -> create Grafana draft with the PromQL above + heatmap prototype (ETA: Tue)
- sandeep -> add a stable metric name for batch_saturation_ratio and a low-card label set (model only for verified models, region, pool) (ETA: Wed)
- ashley -> confirm ingestion cost / sample rate policy and set telemetry alerts if cost exceeds threshold (ETA: Thu)
- nora -> provide mockups and fallback copy for missing data (ETA: Tue)

deploy-bot: deploy job queued for telemetry-config branch (#482) — status: queued :hourglass_flowing_sand:

nora: one more: can we include a boolean metric indicating when the batcher is in fallback mode (e.g., forced single-request flush)? would make rollouts UX easier.

sandeep: yes — we'll add batch_fallback_mode{pool,reason} gauge (0/1). We'll keep reason low-card ("overloaded","config-change","degraded-kernel").

jamie: great. If nobody objects I'll spin up the Grafana draft and tag everyone when ready. :thumbsup:

ashley: :thumbsup: blocking only on final sample rates, but good to go otherwise.

sandeep: will open a small PR to add the stable metric names and document expected cardinality in the telemetry README.

jamie: thanks all — keeping this thread as the single source of truth for Console batching panel scope and telemetry constraints.
